title: A very simple program may underlie all of physics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A very simple program may underlie all of physics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Underneath the known laws of physics there may be a single very simple program from which all known laws, and all the complexity of the universe, emerge.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Underneath the laws of physics as we know them today it could be that there lies a very simple program from which all the known laws—and ultimately all the complexity we see in the universe—emerges.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “The Problems of Physics” (from p. 433), p. 434. Scope: the fundamental laws of the universe

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-01: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.10

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: As stated, the hypothesis is existential and modal rather than a concrete physical model. Existing physical data could test specified candidates but cannot confirm or refute that an unspecified program may exist. Operationalizing it would require adding content not present in the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A particular candidate program could be tested by deriving quantitative physical predictions and comparing them with observations, but the existential statement that some unspecified simple program may underlie all physics supplies no unique prediction or falsifying outcome.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No candidate program or complexity threshold is specified.

Failure of any finite set of candidates cannot refute existence of another.

Known laws and all complexity do not define a finite empirical criterion.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.08
data adequacy: 0.08
discriminating power: 0.05
data existence: 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The wording is modal: there could be a simple underlying program. Until a definite program is proposed, every dataset is consistent with the claim and with its denial. Similar-looking simulations would not test it, and no public resource distinguishes this hypothesis from rival foundations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: As stated, the claim asserts only that there may be some very simple program from which known physics emerges. No particular program, observable, or contradicting outcome is specified, so no measurement confirms or refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A hedged existence claim is compatible both with every current observation and with the failure to exhibit such a program.

Matching a simple program to all of known physics would require a specific candidate that the claim does not provide.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.1
discriminating power: 0.1
